heading: 8.5 Unit assertion function
text:
### 8.5 Unit assertion function [LUNI.8.5]

Asserting a number into a unit type and stripping a unit back to a number are
`::` conversion casts ([LCST.4.5.2]). The number is of the kind the unit's
dimension stores ([LUNI.8.7.3]): `Float` for a `float64` dimension, `Int` for an
`int64` or `int32` one. Both casts are total.

`<number> → <unit>` takes the number as being in that unit: the result is the
value that number names, held in the base unit ([LUNI.7.2]), so `35.0::celsius`
is 35 `celsius` and `5::second` is 5 seconds. [RLOW.6.1.10] states how it lowers.

`<unit> → <number>` strips the dimension and is an identity at runtime. It applies
to a unit-typed value and a dimension-typed value ([LUNI.7.1]) alike, and yields
the stored base-unit number. A strip and an assertion into the dimension's base
unit are inverses. A strip followed by an assertion into any other unit reads the
base-unit number as a number in that unit.

A source of any other kind, such as a `String` asserted into a unit, has no
conversion and is refused as an undefined pair ([LCST.4.5.3]).

Assigning a number to a unit-typed field without the `::<unit>` assertion is a
compiler error; the message suggests the cast form.
